clue.text: They are buried in peace

parts.note: the idiom for ending a quarrel speaks of burying small axes, so these tools go underground when peace is made

explanation.surface: Sounds like a line about the dead resting in peace in a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buried in peace' suggests a funeral, but the idiom is burying the hatchet: settling a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: making peace is called burying the hatchet, so small axes are what is buried.

clue.text: Relaxed reception

definitions.meaning: feeling comfortable and easy, as in your own house
an informal party held in one's own house for guests

explanation.surface: A laid-back welcome party.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: comfortable and at ease, and a noun for a party where hosts receive visitors in their house.

clue.text: Stop small company taking fifty on

parts.note: CO is the short form of company
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A small firm is told to halt its plan to hire fifty more staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is an old name for a punctuation mark, and this two-dot mark is one such pause.

clue.text: Dine out on hot food when up in northern capital

indicators.note: out signals the letters of dine are put out of order
in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Eating out on hot food when visiting a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DINE into EDIN; 'up' reverses H + GRUB to give BURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's capital city lies in the north of Britain.

clue.text: Mix a cocktail, say, and get fish in to eat

indicators.note: in tells us the fish goes inside the word for eating

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper or take food
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A bartender mixes drinks and then has some fish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate a cocktail shaker is to mix its contents vigorously; the ', say' marks a cocktail as one example.

clue.text: Cracked a nut, go for something sweet

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Having cracked a nut, someone reaches for a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, so a kind of sweet.

clue.text: When the devil drives, they must

definitions.text: When the devil drives, they must

parts.words: When the devil drives, they must
parts.note: completes the proverb about doing what circumstances force: these must when the devil drives

explanation.surface: A twist on the old proverb about the devil compelling us.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverb completion: the saying runs that necessities must when the devil drives.

clue.text: Was inadequate as an air gunner and fell short as a pilot

definitions.text: Was inadequate as an air gunner
definitions.meaning: a gunner who fired below the target, under it
a pilot who touched down short of the runway

explanation.surface: A wartime aircrew member and pilot both failing at their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: aimed too low when firing, and landed before reaching the runway.

clue.text: Its members draw on the master's guidance

definitions.text: Its members draw on the master's guidance

parts.words: Its members draw on the master's guidance
parts.note: draw on suggests relying on, but here pupils literally draw, sketching under a teacher's instruction

explanation.surface: A group relying on advice from its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw on' reads as relying on; it is literal drawing, and the master is the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Students in a drawing and painting lesson sketch under their teacher's instruction.

clue.text: It sounds quite cold but it may be hot

indicators.note: sounds says the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: chilly means rather cold

explanation.surface: A paradox: something that sounds cold yet is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepper pod that can be fiercely spicy, hot in flavour rather than temperature.

clue.text: Dance around on broken toe? Might make a good story

indicators.note: around signals the letters of dance are moved about
broken means the letters of toe are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dancing on a broken toe would have a tale to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance' looks like the activity, but both 'around' and 'broken' are anagram signals, each working on the word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing account of a real incident is a type of story.

clue.text: Willing scholar returned to provide means

indicators.note: returned means the scholar's letters are turned back to front

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar's degree
to enable is to give the means to do something

explanation.surface: A scholar comes back, keen to fund something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone readily agreeable or responsive is willing.

clue.text: Quiet little brook anything but quiet

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A peaceful little stream that turns out to be noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing high-pitched sound is the opposite of silent, so loud and piercing.

clue.text: Welcome salesman, game to go back and pursue easier way to pay?

parts.note: hi is a greeting of welcome
a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: to go back means the game's letters are written in reverse

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to chase is to pursue

explanation.surface: Greeting a salesman and chasing a deal for an easier payment plan.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) reversed gives UR. Hire purchase is the British term for buying on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying by instalments while using the goods spreads the cost, which is meant to make buying easier.

clue.text: Powerless to get substandard player suspended

parts.note: a ham is a poor, overacting actor
strung up means hung or suspended

explanation.surface: A poor sportsman suspended from the team and left powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, but it is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally with leg tendons cut, so figuratively crippled and unable to act.

clue.text: Yard chase forged money

indicators.note: forged means shaped anew, so the letters of yard chase are recast

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard pursues counterfeit cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash available immediately to spend is money in hand.

clue.text: Title that's used in all-in wrestling?

definitions.text: Title that's used in all-in wrestling?

parts.words: Title that's used in all-in wrestling?
parts.note: title is legal ownership of property; read whimsically, a grip with no restrictions suits no-rules wrestling

explanation.surface: Asks what championship belt is fought for in freestyle wrestling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' looks like a championship; it is legal title to land, punned as an unrestricted grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright ownership of land with no time limit is a form of legal title.

clue.text: Immediately how one knows that someone is surprised

definitions.meaning: right from the beginning, at once

definitions.text: how one knows that someone is surprised
definitions.meaning: a startled person gives a jump, so one knows from that jump

explanation.surface: Spotting someone's surprise straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: from the very beginning, and a pun on a sudden jump betraying surprise.

clue.text: Gloomy study son makes blue

parts.note: sad means gloomy
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: A melancholy boy in his study sinks into depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means depressed, so to make someone blue is to depress them.

clue.text: Local vet in a shambles

indicators.note: in a shambles means in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The neighbourhood vet's surgery is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'in a shambles' is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone born in a place is a local of it.

clue.text: Pay to stay

definitions.meaning: to make one's home and remain somewhere

explanation.surface: A demand for payment in return for lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to clear an account, and to take up residence or remain.

clue.text: A long time to muse

parts.note: an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: Someone spends ages musing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb, to ponder; it is one of the Greek goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts, the Muse of love poetry.

clue.text: Retired people won't get such a fanciful idea

definitions.text: Retired people won't get such a fanciful idea

parts.words: Retired people won't get such a fanciful idea
parts.note: retired here means gone to bed, so their dreams happen at night rather than in waking hours

explanation.surface: Pensioners lacking flights of fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners; it means gone to bed, where dreams come at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant waking fantasy, so a fanciful idea dreamt while not asleep.

clue.text: One can't see what it offers as entertainment

definitions.text: One can't see what it offers as entertainment

parts.words: One can't see what it offers as entertainment
parts.note: broadcast sound only, so its programmes are heard and not watched

explanation.surface: A complaint about entertainment one cannot watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound-only broadcast medium offers programmes listeners hear but never view.

clue.text: Clumsy lout made to tone down remarks?

indicators.note: clumsy means awkwardly put together, so the letters of lout made are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An oafish man is told to soften what he says.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary or soften the pitch of one's voice, so to moderate how things are said.

clue.text: Astronaut found in local, drinking

indicators.note: found in tells us the name sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A famous space traveller spotted drinking in his local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British pub near home.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz Aldrin was the second man to walk on the Moon, an Apollo 11 crew member.

clue.text: Slow movement gets a soldier in trouble

indicators.note: in tells us the a and soldier are placed within the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier moving slowly lands himself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term: a section of a work played at a leisurely tempo.

clue.text: A glass ship

definitions.meaning: a large drinking glass, for sherry or beer
a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rig and two or more masts

explanation.surface: Sounds like a ship made of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tall drinking vessel, and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel.
